name: .357 Auto Express
description:
The .357 Auto Express is GLMZ 2200's answer to a question that has been asked since the early twenty-first century: what if you could get magnum-level performance from a semi-automatic pistol without stepping up to a longer cartridge? The round draws lineage from the .357 SIG and several competing high-pressure bottleneck pistol cartridges developed between 2020 and 2080, consolidated by Arcturus Defense Solutions into a unified spec that now feeds in a family of ADS-pattern service pistols and licensed derivatives. The case is shorter than its revolver-caliber cousin but runs at significantly higher pressure, pushing a .357-diameter projectile to velocities that genuinely challenge light ballistic armor — the kind worn by Tier 2-3 security personnel and increasingly by mid-tier civilians who can afford the augmentation.

In GLMZ's stratified threat landscape, the .357 Auto Express occupies a specific cultural position: it is the round that Mids carry when they want corps-level stopping power in a form factor that doesn't announce itself. Arcturus Civil Security's plainclothes units carry it. So do the better-equipped fixers, the mid-tier corporate troubleshooters who move between access zones and need to be taken seriously by people who would laugh at a nine. The recoil is sharp and the platforms are more expensive than 9x19mm equivalents, which keeps it out of the lowest tiers. But for those who can handle it and afford it, the .357 Auto Express is a significant step up in both capability and statement.
compatibility_note: Compatible with semi-automatic pistols chambered for .357 Auto Express spec, primarily Arcturus Defense Solutions ADS-pattern service pistols and licensed derivatives. Not compatible with .357 Magnum revolver cylinders without a purpose-built conversion. Some high-spec PDW platforms accept it. Caseless variant available in ADS-contract production; brass-cased dominant in civilian gray market.
reliability_note: Very reliable in platforms designed for it. High-pressure operation requires tighter manufacturing tolerances and more consistent maintenance than 9x19mm, but modern production brass-cased .357 AE is highly dependable. More sensitive to chamber fouling than lower-pressure rounds — platforms shooting it need regular cleaning. No energy dependency. Caseless variant is reliable in ADS-spec chambers.
